markdown_report:
At 10% progress, prioritize a small, falsifiable intervention: test whether an explicit recent-history residual improves the unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Electronics has a 14.95% training negative-win rate versus 3.03% for Movies_and_TV. This motivates category-specific analysis but does not establish generalization failure. (2) Embedding alignment scores cluster near 0.54–0.56 while margins differ substantially. Aggregate embedding geometry therefore cannot explain the observed separation differences alone. (3) User feedback identifies unsupported current-purpose assumptions and overextended older interests. This motivates testing recent evidence, without treating recency as proof of intent.

**Insights from related work.** (1) History-shuffling studies motivate testing sequence dependence [1]. Sensitivity alone cannot establish useful dependence. (2) Padding and positional encoding can change recommendation performance [2,3]. Perturbations must therefore separate item changes from position and mask changes. (3) Sampled metrics can change model ordering [4]. Auxiliary catalog diagnostics must remain separate from the pinned selection objective.

**Framework and directions.** Organize experiments along three axes: evidence source (latest item, recent window, older history), intervention (identity replacement, order permutation, representation residual), and outcome (training diagnostic, fixed-candidate validation, auxiliary catalog audit). This connects controlled diagnosis, minimal architecture changes, and diagnostic predictive validity. The principal gap is whether a diagnostic observation predicts a useful intervention.

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality / future potential / code difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Controlled perturbation calibration: 4/7/3.** Originality: isolates confounds, but extends existing shuffle tests. Potential: improves interpretability, but cannot improve rankings directly. Difficulty: needs few model changes, but requires carefully matched controls.
- **Recent-history residual: 4/8/4.** Originality: links diagnosis to intervention, but residual pooling is conventional. Potential: directly tests current-interest modeling, but recent purchases may already satisfy a need. Difficulty: reuses embeddings, but requires consistent training and predictor changes.
- **Popularity-mixed negative sampling: 3/6/3.** Originality: supplies stronger competitors, but is established practice. Potential: tests weak separation, but may misalign with uniform evaluation candidates. Difficulty: sampling is simple, but exclusion and false-negative handling require care [4].

**Selected algorithm: controlled recent-history residual.** For every causal training prefix, form its SASRec state h and an exponentially weighted mean r of its last five nonpadding item embeddings. Score items using q = h + αr, preserving the existing scoring scale and loss. Prespecify α ∈ {0, 0.1, 0.3}; retain identical preprocessing, seeds, training schedules, and all four dataset routes.

Pseudocode: `h = SASRec(prefix); r = recent_pool(prefix); q = h + alpha*r; optimize(existing_loss(score(q)))`.

Before evaluation, record the hypothesis that preserving recent identities matters more than matched older replacements. Compare each arm through the host’s pinned validation protocol; report category differences and paired uncertainty when available. Preserve `DiagnosisProbe`, adapt feature hooks and predictor serialization, and generate the required unseen-item recommendations. No improvement is claimed before measurement.

idea.description: Test a minimal recent-history residual added to SASRec, using controlled history perturbations to state a directional hypothesis before measuring the intervention under pinned macro validation HR@10.
idea.motivation: The supplied user diagnosis suggests broad affinity sometimes overwhelms evidence of current interest. Training margins reveal category differences but cannot establish this mechanism or predict validation gains. A small residual provides a feasible intervention at 10% research progress.
idea.implementation_notes: Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four categories and dataset routing, and the environment-controlled SASREC_EPOCHS default of 200. Use identical baseline loss, optimizer, schedule, and checkpoint policy across arms. Pool the last five valid item embeddings with normalized weights proportional to exp(-j), where j=0 is most recent; return zero for an empty prefix. Apply the residual causally at each training position and at final-state inference. Prespecify alpha values 0, 0.1, and 0.3, subject to the remaining shared GPU budget. Update the predictor writer and saved configuration to reconstruct the trained architecture. Keep view.model as the actual module; expose residual-enhanced states through log2feats and matching scores through predict_score. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device) and run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Retain embedding and training-margin diagnostics, model-state restoration, and explicit unavailable values for unsupported metadata. Calibrate perturbations with unchanged-input, last-item-only, and popularity-score controls. Use position-preserving replacements and permutations that preserve the final item, length, mask, and item multiset where applicable. Generate full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for five real training users per category, using only allowed data. Select solely by independently evaluated four-category macro validation HR@10; auxiliary diagnostics and simulator feedback remain explanatory.
idea.pseudocode:
prespecify alpha_grid = [0.0, 0.1, 0.3]
record diagnostic hypothesis before inspecting intervention validation results
for alpha in alpha_grid, subject to remaining search budget:
    initialize baseline SASRec with training seed 42
    for each unchanged training batch:
        h = sasrec.log2feats(sequence)
        r = causal_recent_embedding_pool(sequence, window=5, weights=exp(-age))
        features = h + alpha * r
        optimize unchanged loss using features and existing item scorer
    save architecture configuration, checkpoint, and matching predictor
    run compatible training diagnostics with state restoration
    obtain pinned host validation HR@10 for every category
compare macro HR@10 and category regressions
select checkpoint using only the prescribed validation objective

originality.positive: Connects controlled history diagnostics to a prespecified, directly testable architectural intervention.
originality.negative: Recent embedding pooling and residual representations are conventional; novelty rests mainly on the diagnostic-to-intervention protocol.

future_potential.positive: Provides a reproducible way to test whether apparent recent-interest failures correspond to an actionable modeling limitation.
future_potential.negative: Recency may reflect completed purchases or transient needs, and diagnostic sensitivity may fail to predict validation improvements.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses SASRec embeddings and scoring with a small causal pooling operation and a scalar coefficient.
code_difficulty.negative: Training-position causality, compatibility hooks, predictor serialization, and controlled perturbations must agree exactly.

related_work.title: [1] Does It Look Sequential?
contributions: Studies history shuffling in sequential recommendation, motivating direct tests of sequence dependence.
limitations: Shuffle sensitivity alone does not establish beneficial recent-history use or validate the proposed residual.

related_work.title: [2] Repeated Padding
contributions: Shows that padding choices can materially affect sequential recommendation performance.
limitations: Does not establish that observed deletion effects arise from lost preference evidence rather than altered representation.

related_work.title: [3] CAPE
contributions: Investigates positional encoding choices, supporting explicit controls for item-position assignments.
limitations: Does not establish the predictive validity of the proposed perturbation protocol.

related_work.title: [4] On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Demonstrates limitations of sampled recommendation metrics, including potential changes in model ordering.
limitations: Does not identify which intervention will improve this benchmark; its pinned sampled metric remains the required selection objective.
